title: Tax-loss harvesting in your taxable account
summary: Realize losses to offset gains and up to $3,000 of ordinary income per year. Excess losses carry forward indefinitely.
detailsHtml:
The mechanics

When a position in your taxable account drops below your cost basis, you sell it to realize the loss, then immediately buy a similar-but-not-identical replacement to maintain market exposure. The loss offsets realized capital gains; up to $3,000 of excess loss offsets ordinary income (taxed at your marginal rate, which is higher than capital gains rates — so this is a rate-arbitrage).

The wash sale rule

You cannot buy "substantially identical" securities within 30 days before or after the loss sale (a 61-day window). This rule applies across all your accounts including IRAs and your spouse's accounts. Selling VTSAX and buying ITOT is generally considered safe (different funds, different indexes, different providers); selling VTSAX and buying VTI in another account is not (same fund, same provider).

The IRA trap: If you sell at a loss in your taxable account and buy the same security in your IRA within 31 days, the loss is disallowed and is NOT added to the IRA's cost basis (per IRS Revenue Ruling 2008-5). You forfeit the loss entirely. Coordinate across accounts.

Empirical value

Vanguard and Wealthfront research estimates the annual after-tax alpha from systematic TLH at 0.2–1.0%, with higher values in volatile markets and for higher-bracket investors. The strategy compounds over decades.
